entries.findings:
• Network meta-analysis (Sports Medicine, Jul 2025, PMID 40791980) found autoregulated methods (APRE, RPE, VBT) all outperform fixed-load progression for 1RM strength gains, with APRE ranking highest (SUCRA 93%) and RPE-based methods also significantly better than fixed loading (SUCRA 66.8%).
• JSSE 2025 (Martikainen et al.) found similar strength/hypertrophy outcomes when training continuously close to failure vs. varying proximity-to-failure (RIR cycling) in resistance-trained lifters, supporting flexible RPE targets over rigid rep-max prescriptions.
• Nov 2025 study on RIR estimation accuracy found lifters estimate reps-in-reserve more accurately at higher effort levels (RPE 8-10 / RIR 0-2) and higher intensities, meaning autoregulation is more reliable late in a set/session than early.
• Schoenfeld et al. (Sports Medicine) frequency data reaffirmed: training each muscle group ~2x/week outperforms 1x/week at equated volume, and hypertrophy continues to rise with weekly hard-set volume (10+ sets/muscle/week), supporting the 6-day PPL x2 frequency structure.
• Tandfonline 2024/2025 follow-up found training to failure vs. leaving RIR produced similar hypertrophy over 8 weeks in trained lifters, suggesting RPE 7-9 autoregulated sets are sufficient without needing to push to failure every session.
entries.recommended_change: Keep RPE 7-9 (not RPE 10/failure) as the default autoregulation target for accessory work, reserving RPE 9-10 for weekly top sets on compounds to match APRE/RPE-superiority findings while minimizing fatigue accumulation across the 6-day split.
